The problem involves a train passing two men walking in opposite directions. The key is to correctly interpret the relative motion and timing.

Let train length = L, train speed = v_t, first man speed = v_1, second man speed = v_2.

Train passes first man (same direction) in 20 s: L = 20(v_t - v_1).  
Train passes second man (opposite direction) in 18 s: L = 18(v_t + v_2).  
Equating: 20(v_t - v_1) = 18(v_t + v_2) → 2v_t = 20v_1 + 18v_2 → v_t = 10v_1 + 9v_2.

The train meets the second man 10 minutes (600 s) after passing the first man. At the moment the train passes the first man, the distance between the two men is D. The train closes this distance relative to the second man at speed v_t + v_2 in 600 s, so D = 600(v_t + v_2).

After the train passes the second man, the remaining distance between the men is D minus the distance they closed during those 600 s. They close at speed v_1 + v_2, so distance closed = 600(v_1 + v_2). Remaining distance = 600(v_t + v_2) - 600(v_1 + v_2) = 600(v_t - v_1).

From L = 20(v_t - v_1), we get v_t - v_1 = L/20. So remaining distance = 600 * L/20 = 30L.

We need v_1 + v_2. From L = 20(v_t - v_1) and L = 18(v_t + v_2), subtract: (v_t + v_2) - (v_t - v_1) = v_1 + v_2 = L/18 - L/20 = L/180.

Time to meet after train passes second man = remaining distance / (v_1 + v_2) = 30L / (L/180) = 30 * 180 = 5400 s = 90 minutes.

Thus the correct answer is 90 minutes, which is option b.
